description: Catch-all for any batchNumber that is not one of the two real Ashton batches: returns 0 hits, which is exactly what the live tool does for a nonexistent batch (a nil under a batch means the batch is wrong, not that the parish is empty). ORDER: after the two exact batch fixtures, BEFORE the name-search fixture. Without it, a call carrying an invented batch AND the name arguments satisfies the name predicate (subset matching) and comes back with 13,069 hits — the test would reward a fabricated batch number, against its own pass condition that the batch must come off a returned result.
